\section*{Question 1}
\begin{itemize}
\item[] Let \(R\) be the region bounded by the \(y\)-axis and the graphs of \(y=\frac{x^{3}}{1+x^{2}}\) and \(y=4-2 x\), as shown in the figure above.
\item[(a)] Find the area of \(R\).
\item[(b)] Find the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is revolved about the \(x\)-axis.
(c) The region \(R\) is the base of a solid. For this solid, each cross section perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis is a square. Find the volume of this solid.
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/f8e387be-64d1-44b5-b4b5-c2a6303bd6cd-1.jpg?height=509&width=554&top_left_y=382&top_left_x=1392)
\end{itemize}

Region \(R\)
\[
\frac{x^{3}}{1+x^{2}}=4-2 x \text { at } x=1.487664=A
\]
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text { Area } & =\int_{0}^{A}\left(4-2 x-\frac{x^{3}}{1+x^{2}}\right) d x \\
& =3.214 \text { or } 3.215
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] Volume
\[
\begin{aligned}
& =\pi \int_{0}^{A}\left((4-2 x)^{2}-\left(\frac{x^{3}}{1+x^{2}}\right)^{2}\right) d x \\
& =31.884 \text { or } 31.885 \text { or } 10.149 \pi
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text { Volume } & =\int_{0}^{A}\left(4-2 x-\frac{x^{3}}{1+x^{2}}\right)^{2} d x \\
& =8.997
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[1] : Correct limits in an integral in (a), (b), or (c).
\end{itemize}
